classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that each path is determined by one non-corner point on each side and that all four point choices are independent.

content.prompt: Consider a $5\times5$ grid of unit squares as shown below. An ant starts at a grid point on side $AB$. She visits all three sides $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$ in that order before returning to her starting position. She does not visit any of the vertices $A$, $B$, $C$ or $D$. Her journey forms a quadrilateral. How many different paths can the ant take?

spec.description: Unshaded five-by-five grid with all sixteen non-corner boundary points, outside corner labels and a blue supplied sample quadrilateral. A blank-grid template cannot express the boundary markers, corner labels and sample path.
spec.answerVisibility: The sample path is a permanent given; no answer count appears in the student diagram.

inlines.text: There are four choices on each of the four sides.

answer.worked:
Each side has four non-corner grid points. Choose the starting point on $AB$, then one point on each of $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$. These choices determine the quadrilateral and its return to the starting point.

$$\begin{align*}N&=4\times4\times4\times4\\N&=4^4\\N&=256.\end{align*}$$

There are 256 different paths.
